QF.id: AIFM CIII AIFs in India and Suitability_5

question.text: Ms. Anjali Menon, aged 35, is a salaried professional with a portfolio of INR 40 lakh and seeks liquidity within 18 months for a house purchase. A bank RM pitches a Category III AIF. Per the chapter's suitability framework, why is Cat III UNSUITABLE here?

answer.text: Cat III funds invest only in unlisted early-stage ventures with a 10-year lockup
Cat III funds are only available to non-resident investors under FEMA Notification 355/2015
She fails the minimum investment threshold of INR 1 crore and the investor profile (liquidity horizon less than 3 years, non-HNI)
Cat III funds must be held for at least 7 years under SEBI close-ended structure rules

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 4.4.1 states Cat III AIFs are suited only for institutional investors, family offices, non-resident investors and UHNI/HNI. Minimum investment is INR 1 crore (except AIF employees at INR 25 lakh). Cat III funds have a minimum tenure of 3 years and investors seeking liquidity within 3 years are expressly told AIFs are unsuitable due to the illiquidity factor. Ms. Menon fails both the ticket size and horizon tests. The Trap: Option A confuses Cat III (listed-market + derivatives) with Cat I VCF. Option B is false — Cat III is open to resident HNIs, FPIs and NRIs. Option D invents a 7-year rule; Cat III minimum tenure is 3 years. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) asks the same suitability question from the sales side. XIX-E asks it from the Manager's onboarding/KYC perspective — you must refuse subscriptions below INR 1 crore and document unsuitability red flags. Manager's Pro-Tip: Build a pre-subscription suitability questionnaire capturing ticket size, horizon, experience with derivatives, and liquidity needs. SEBI's inspections scrutinise whether the AIF Manager knowingly onboarded unsuitable investors — fund-level penalties apply.
